NWSheadline: FLASH FLOOD WARNING WILL EXPIRE AT 1 AM CDT EARLY THIS MORNING FOR SOUTH CENTRAL STARR COUNTY

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 2 at 12:04AM CDT until October 2 at 1:00AM CDT by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
FFWBRO

The National Weather Service in Brownsville has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
South Central Starr County in deep south Texas...

* Until 100 AM CDT.

* At 1204 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain across the
warned area. Between 4 and 8 inches of rain have fallen. Additional
rainfall amounts up to 1.5 inches are possible in the warned area.
Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by heavy rain.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Rio Grande City, Garciasville, La Grulla, La Puerta, La Victoria,
Santa Cruz, Alto Bonito, Las Lomas, Ringgold Middle School, Fort
Ringgold County Park, Rio Grande City Fire Department, Starr County
Sheriffs Office, Grulla Middle School, Rio Grande City Municipal
Airport, Starr County Memorial Hospital, Los Alvarez, Los Garzas,
La Casita and Rio Grande City Library.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.
